1 1.

The instant appeal has been preferred by the appellants-claimants for enhancement of the compensation awarded by the judgment and award dated 19.07.2018 passed by the learned MACT,
(Labour Court), Churu in MAC Case No.72/2016 whereby the learned Tribunal partly allowed the claim petition and awarded Rs.10,74,000/- to the claimants @ 6 per cent per annum as interest.

2. Brief facts of the case are that the appellants-claimants filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ('The [2024:RJ-JD:33692] (2 of 7) [CMA-2248/2018] Act of 1988')
before the learned MACT, (Labour Court), Churu against the respondents-non-claimants wherein, it has been averred that on 25.03.2013, Praveen (since deceased) was going from hotel to factory for buying milk along with petitioner No.2- Mangi Lal by his motorcycle bearing No. RJ 10 SC 5877, at 3: 00 AM, when they reached at Shri Handicraft Factory situated at Sardarshahar to Bikaner Road,
then a truck bearing Reg. No.RJ 07 GC 2391 ('offending vehicle') driven in a rash and negligent manner, came from wrong side and hit the motorcycle due to which, Mangilal fell towards the road side and Praveen fell down headlong on the road and suffered grievous injuries and deceased Praveen succumbed to death.
Thereafter, a police complaint was also lodged against the respondent No.3 herein and a challan came to be filed.

The respondent No.2 was the owner of the offending vehicle, the respondent No.1 was the Insurance Company and the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.1-Insurance Company and the liability to pay the payment was fastened upon the insurance company.

3. The respondent Nos.2 and 3 were summoned before the learned Tribunal and reply was filed on their behalf to the claim petition wherein it was stated that the said accident occurred due to the negligence on part of the claimants and the claimants have wrongly mentioned the age and income of the deceased in the claim petition.
It was further submitted that the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent- insurance company and that, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the claimants.
Thus, they urged for dismissal of the claim petition.

4. The respondent No.1, Insurance Company was also summoned before the learned Tribunal and also filed reply to the claim petition [2024:RJ-JD:33692] (3 of 7) [CMA-2248/2018] wherein, it was stated that the claimaints have wrongly mentioned the age and income of the deceased in the claim petition and that, at the time of accident, the driver was not having valid and effective driving license.

It was further submitted that the insured vehicle was used as a commercial purpose,
therefore, there is a violation of insurance policy, and thus the insurance company is not liable to pay any amount of compensation.
Thus, the insurance company craved for dismissal of the claim petition.

5. As per the pleadings and the material available on record, the learned Tribunal framed the following issues :-

sentences.text: Both the parties adduced, oral as well as documentary evidence and after hearing both the parties, learned Tribunal awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.10,74,000/- to the claimants on account of death of deceased Praveen vide judgment and award dated 19.07.2018 and, thus, being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the same, the instant misc. appeal has been preferred.

7. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the impugned judgment and award dated 19.07.2018 has been passed in a cryptic and arbitrary manner and is against the settled proposition of law and [2024:RJ-JD:33692] (4 of 7)
[CMA-2248/2018] hence, the same deserves to the modified.

In this regard, he submits that it is an admitted position that at the time of the accident, Praveen (since deceased) rendered his service as a Superwiser in Shri Handicraft Factory,
Sardarshahar and was earning a sum of Rs.8,000/- as a monthly salary.

Besides that,
he used to get food and lodging expenses separately, but the learned Tribunal failed to conclude the income of deceased Praveen while taking future prospects into consideration and the learned Tribunal based it judgment and award on conjecture and summaries and awarded only a meager amount in head of earning.
He also submits that the deceased was earning a good income but the learned Tribunal failed to consider the same, which is bad in the eyes of law.

8. Learned counsel for the appellants further submits that the learned Tribunal overlooked the heading of future prospects, as the deceased was having bright a future ahead and the learned Tribunal has not provided the amount of compensation under the aforestated heading.
He also submits that a meagre amount was awarded to the appellants-claimants under the head of 'Damages', 'Mental Agony', 'Love and Affection' and 'Funeral Expenses'.

Learned counsel for the appellants-claimants thus,
urges that the impugned judgment and award dated 19.07.2018 passed by the learned MACT (Labour Court), Churu deserves to be modified and the amount of compensation may be enhanced.

sentences.text:
Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent-insurance company vehemently opposes the submissions advanced at Bar by the learned counsel for the appellants-claimants and submits that the instant misc.
appeal warrants rejection.

He also submits that Handicraft factory has no agreement with deceased Praveen in regard to the salary and there [2024:RJ-JD:33692] (5 of 7) [CMA-2248/2018] is no such documents to prove the salary certificate of the deceased.
He also submits that deceased was also a semi skilled labour.
10. I have given my thoughtful consideration to the submissions advanced at Bar by the learned counsel for the parties and have gone through the material placed on record.

11. It is apparent on the face of the record that the deceased at the time of accident, was 23 years of age and was earning way more than what was assessed by the learned Tribunal while determining income of the deceased, as the deceased was having every likelihood of advancement in his career,
thus, the learned Tribunal has wrongfully assessed the income of the deceased while keeping in view the prevalent minimum wages at the time of accident which is not agreed by this Court.
Hence, this Court finds considerable force in the arguments advanced by the appellants-claimants with regard to the assessment of the income of the deceased.

12. Since, there is no dispute on the factual matrix of the case, both the counsels were directed to submit a calculation of the compensation awarded to the claimants afresh in light of the guidelines as laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the Cases of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. : (2017)16 SCC 680, and Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation : AIR 2009 SC 3104.

 [2024:RJ-JD:33692] (6 of 7) [CMA-2248/2018]
TOTAL  15,96,672/-

4  after deduction)
(15,96,672-5,32,224) =10,64,448/-
(Add) 48,000/- x 3 1,44,000/-
(Add) Funeral & loss of estate 36,000/-
(18,000+18,000)
TOTAL(10,64,448+1,44,000+36000) 12,44,478/-
(Less) Already awarded by Tribunal 10,74,000/-
Enhanced Amount (round figure) 1,70,448/-
14.

Accordingly, the instant misc. appeal is partly allowed in the above terms and the judgment/award dated 19.07.2018 passed by the learned Judge, MACT, (Labour Court), Churu, in MAC Case No.72/2016, is partially modified accordingly.
The enhanced amount of 1,70,448/- shall carry interest @ 6% per annum from the date of filing of claim petition till the date of deposit.

The enhanced amount shall be deposited by the respondent-Insurance Company with the learned Tribunal within a period of six weeks from today failing which, the interest shall stand enhanced @
7.5% per annum from the date of this order till actual realization.

This Court also observes that since the amount awarded under consortium, funeral expenses and loss of estates already carries an increase of 10% every 3 years, therefore, the said headings shall not carry the interest amount, in accordance with the judgment passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case of Rasal Kanwar Vs. Harish Chand (S.B. Civil Misc. Appeal No.1099/2019) decided on 20.03.2024.
15.

sentences.text:
Thus, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the enhanced amount, i.e. Rs.
1,70,448/- to appellants/claimants.
Any [2024:RJ-JD:33692] (7 of 7) [CMA-2248/2018] amount already paid by the respondents, shall be adjusted towards the amount finally awarded by this Court.

16. No order as to costs.
17. Record be returned to the Tribunal forthwith.
